passages.note: House Third Reading roll call naming Nguyen Y on a single-subject athletics bill; 24 No of 60 voting, so not near-unanimous.
Bill overview lists Nguyen as a co-sponsor of SB1165, so the bill as filed is his own act as well as his vote.

passages.provision_quote: B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: Chaptered text printing the operative provision; subsection C leaves boys' and coed teams open, which excludes the total-ban rung.

rows.reasoning: Nguyen co-sponsored SB1165 (2022) and voted Y on House Third Reading of it, a single-subject athletics bill that passed 31-24 and so is not near-unanimous. Its operative section designates school teams by biological sex and provides that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" "may not be open to students of the male sex", which is the rung that would "require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth." Subsection C expressly leaves boys' and coed teams open to any student, so the rung that would "completely ban all transgender athletes from competing in any organized sports competitions" is excluded by the bill's own text.
